title: Jordan vs Egypt: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Jordan and Egypt based on Reddit discussions, real costs, safety data, and traveler preferences — Petra vs the Pyramids, Wadi Rum vs the Nile, and everything in between.

categories.title: 🏺 Historic Sites & Icons
categories.summary: Petra vs the Pyramids — two of the greatest archaeological sites on earth. Jordan offers the Rose-Red City carved from sandstone cliffs, revealed at the end of the dramatic Siq canyon. Egypt offers the Great Pyramids of Giza, the last surviving Wonder of the Ancient World.
highlights: Jordan: Petra has 800+ monuments across 264 square kilometers, including the Treasury, Monastery, and Royal Tombs. Jerash is one of the world's best-preserved Roman cities.
Egypt: The Great Pyramid of Khufu is 146 meters tall, 4,500 years old. The Grand Egyptian Museum (2023) is now the world's largest. Luxor's Valley of the Kings has 70+ royal tombs.

categories.title: 🌄 Nature & Landscape
categories.summary: Jordan wins on landscape variety packed into a compact trip: Wadi Rum desert, Dead Sea float, and Red Sea diving. Egypt offers the Nile, Red Sea resorts, and the Sahara.
highlights: Jordan: Wadi Rum overnight Bedouin camps (-150/person), Dead Sea floating (lowest point on earth), Aqaba Red Sea diving with 20-30m visibility.
Egypt: Nile cruises (-200/day), Hurghada and Dahab diving, Mt. Sinai sunrise hike, White Desert formations.

categories.title: 💰 Cost Comparison
categories.summary: Egypt is cheaper overall (-60/day mid-range vs -100 in Jordan), but Jordan's Jordan Pass (~ including visa + Petra + 40 sites) closes the gap for most travelers.
highlights: Jordan: Mid-range hotel -100/night, street meal -5, restaurant dinner -20. Jordan Pass saves -100 vs paying separately.
Egypt: Mid-range hotel -70/night, street meal -3, koshari . Attraction fees add up: Pyramids ~, Egyptian Museum ~, Grand Egyptian Museum ~.

categories.title: 🍜 Food & Dining
categories.summary: Both countries offer excellent food at low prices. Jordan: mansaf, mezze, falafel. Egypt: koshari (), ta'ameyya, ful medames. Tie on quality; Egypt wins on price.
highlights: Jordan: Mansaf (lamb in yogurt sauce) is the must-eat national dish. Hashem Restaurant in Amman serves legendary falafel since 1952.
Egypt: Koshari is a  masterpiece of rice, lentils, pasta, tomato sauce, and fried onions. Cairo's street food scene is exceptional.

categories.title: 🚗 Getting Around
categories.summary: Both countries require planning. Jordan: JETT buses + rental car recommended. Egypt: Uber in Cairo is excellent, internal flights connect to Luxor cheaply.

categories.title: 🌤️ Weather & Best Time
categories.summary: Both countries share the same optimal travel window: October through April. Jordan is best March-May (wildflowers in Wadi Rum). Egypt: November-February is the sweet spot.

categories.title: 🛡️ Safety
categories.summary: Jordan wins clearly — one of the safest countries in the Middle East. Egypt is safe but has more tout pressure and harassment reports, especially for solo female travelers.
highlights: Jordan: Reddit reports consistently praise Jordanian hospitality and safety. Solo female travelers report feeling comfortable throughout the country.
Egypt: Safe in tourist zones but aggressive touts at Pyramids and Khan el-Khalili. Hire a licensed guide at major sites to reduce pressure.

categories.title: 🏨 Where to Stay
categories.summary: Jordan: Amman (Jabal Amman district), Wadi Musa for Petra, Wadi Rum Bedouin camps. Egypt: Zamalek (Cairo), Mena House (Pyramid views), Luxor for Valley of the Kings.

categories.title: 🗺️ Day Trips
categories.summary: Egypt wins on day trip depth — Luxor is extraordinary. Jordan's Jerash (Roman city) and King's Highway drive are world-class in their own right.
highlights: Jordan: Jerash (1h, best Roman city outside Italy), Dead Sea, Madaba mosaic, Little Petra (free, fewer crowds).
Egypt: Luxor (1h flight, Valley of the Kings), Saqqara/Dahshur (Step Pyramid, much fewer tourists), Alexandria (2.5h train).

categories.title: 🔀 Why Not Both?
categories.summary: Jordan and Egypt are a natural pair — 1.5h flight Amman-Cairo or 1h ferry Aqaba-Nuweiba. A 12-day Jordan + Egypt trip is one of the greatest Middle East itineraries.

categories.title: 🧭 Decision Framework
categories.summary: Choose Jordan for ease, safety, Petra, and landscape. Choose Egypt for the Pyramids, Nile, Luxor, and budget. Do both if you have 12+ days.

verdict.summary: Jordan for most travelers. Egypt for the Pyramids. Jordan wins on ease, safety, natural scenery, and overall travel experience. Egypt is harder but has the Pyramids of Giza — the only surviving Wonder of the Ancient World — and unmatched historical depth. For smoother travel: Jordan. For the Pyramids: Egypt. Do both if you can.
takeaways: Jordan edge: Safety, ease, Petra, Wadi Rum, Dead Sea, less harassment, overall traveler experience
Egypt edge: The Pyramids (unmatched), Nile cruises, Luxor, Alexandria, cost, historical depth
Best combo: 6 days Jordan → fly to Cairo → 4 days Cairo/Luxor. One of the greatest itineraries in the region

cards.title: Choose Jordan if…
cards.text: You want an incredible, hassle-free Middle East adventure. Petra alone is worth the flight. Add Wadi Rum and the Dead Sea and it's one of the world's top trips.

cards.title: Choose Egypt if…
cards.text: Standing in front of the Great Pyramid is on your bucket list. Nothing on earth looks like it. And Luxor's Valley of the Kings makes the trip even more extraordinary.

cards.title: Do both if…
cards.text: You have 12+ days. Fly Amman → Cairo in 1.5 hours or take the Aqaba–Sinai ferry. This combo is one of the most historically rich itineraries on the planet.

faqs.question: Is Jordan or Egypt better for first-time visitors to the Middle East?
faqs.answer: Jordan is the easier and more comfortable first-time Middle East experience. The country is significantly safer, the people are famously welcoming, and Petra alone justifies the trip. Egypt is more intense but has the Pyramids. Reddit consensus: Jordan first if you're unsure; Egypt if the Pyramids are a bucket-list must.

faqs.question: Which is cheaper: Jordan or Egypt?
faqs.answer: Egypt is cheaper overall — budget travelers spend $25-40/day vs $50-80/day in Jordan. However, Jordan's Jordan Pass (~$108) includes the visa, Petra, and 40+ sites, saving most travelers $50-100 vs paying separately. Egypt's attraction fees (Pyramids ~$20-40, Egyptian Museum ~$16) also add up fast.

faqs.question: Is Petra or the Pyramids better?
faqs.answer: Both are in the top tier of human heritage sites. Petra is more intimate and physical — you hike through the Siq canyon to discover the Treasury. The Pyramids are incomprehensibly old and massive. If you can only do one: Petra edges ahead slightly for the overall day experience, but Egypt's historical depth is unmatched.
